name: Petit Chablis
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Chardonnay dry white. Use INAO for exact production rules.
officialRulesNote: Petit Chablis is an AOC for dry white wines in the Chablis area.
commonPracticeNote: Usually lighter and earlier-drinking than Chablis.

terroir.learningPoint: Cool climate and limestone soils make high-acid Chardonnay with citrus and mineral cues.

examNotes: Chardonnay only in common study shorthand.
Useful contrast with Chablis and Chablis Grand Cru.

name: Chablis
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Chardonnay dry white. Use INAO for official rules.
officialRulesNote: Chablis is an AOC for dry white wines in northern Burgundy.
commonPracticeNote: Typically unoaked or subtly handled, emphasizing acidity, citrus, and mineral character.

terroir.learningPoint: Kimmeridgian limestone and cool climate are central to the classic high-acid, mineral Chablis profile.

examNotes: Contrast with richer Côte de Beaune Chardonnay.

name: Chablis Grand Cru
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Chardonnay dry white. Use INAO for official site rules.
officialRulesNote: Chablis Grand Cru covers the grand cru climats of Chablis.
commonPracticeNote: More concentration, texture, and ageing potential than basic Chablis.
classificationContext: Grand cru level in the Burgundy hierarchy.

terroir.learningPoint: Grand cru exposure and limestone soils give more power while retaining Chablis acidity.

examNotes: More body and age potential than Chablis.

name: Gevrey-Chambertin
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Pinot Noir red Burgundy. Use INAO for exact rules.
officialRulesNote: Gevrey-Chambertin is a Côte de Nuits village appellation.
commonPracticeNote: Often among the firmer, more structured Côte de Nuits village profiles.

terroir.learningPoint: Côte de Nuits limestone and slope position help frame structured Pinot Noir with savory depth.

examNotes: Often taught as structured and powerful by Burgundy standards.

name: Morey-Saint-Denis
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Pinot Noir red Burgundy. Use INAO for official rules.
officialRulesNote: Morey-Saint-Denis is a Côte de Nuits village appellation.
commonPracticeNote: Often positioned stylistically between Gevrey structure and Chambolle elegance.

terroir.learningPoint: Its position between famous neighbors makes it useful for studying Côte de Nuits transitions.

examNotes: Bridge style between Gevrey and Chambolle in study shorthand.

name: Chambolle-Musigny
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Pinot Noir red Burgundy. Use INAO for official rules.
officialRulesNote: Chambolle-Musigny is a Côte de Nuits village appellation.
commonPracticeNote: Often taught as elegant, perfumed, and fine-boned.

terroir.learningPoint: Thin limestone-influenced soils help frame the classic perfume and finesse shorthand.

examNotes: Often described as elegant and floral.

name: Vougeot
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: mainly Pinot Noir red Burgundy, with some white permitted depending on classification/site.
officialRulesNote: Vougeot is a small Côte de Nuits village appellation.
commonPracticeNote: Best known in study context because of Clos de Vougeot nearby.

terroir.learningPoint: Small village geography highlights Burgundy's tight village-by-village hierarchy.

name: Vosne-Romanée
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Pinot Noir red Burgundy. Use INAO for official rules.
officialRulesNote: Vosne-Romanée is a Côte de Nuits village appellation.
commonPracticeNote: Often associated with perfume, spice, silkiness, and major grand cru context.
classificationContext: Home area for some of Burgundy's most famous grand cru names.

terroir.learningPoint: Vosne is crucial for understanding Burgundy's village-to-grand-cru hierarchy.

examNotes: Know for famous grand cru context and spicy perfume.

name: Nuits-Saint-Georges
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Pinot Noir red Burgundy. Use INAO for official rules.
officialRulesNote: Nuits-Saint-Georges is a Côte de Nuits village appellation.
commonPracticeNote: Often firmer and more savory, especially compared with Chambolle or Volnay shorthand.

terroir.learningPoint: A key southern Côte de Nuits village with structured Pinot Noir identity.

name: Aloxe-Corton
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: mostly Pinot Noir village wine; Corton/Corton-Charlemagne grand cru context nearby.
officialRulesNote: Aloxe-Corton is a Côte de Beaune village appellation.
commonPracticeNote: Often firmer and more structured than some Côte de Beaune red villages.
classificationContext: Important for Corton and Corton-Charlemagne context.

terroir.learningPoint: Aloxe marks the northern Côte de Beaune transition and major Corton hill context.

name: Beaune
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: mainly Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay also important in Côte de Beaune.
officialRulesNote: Beaune is a Côte de Beaune village appellation with many premier cru sites.
commonPracticeNote: Often red-fruited, approachable, and important as the historic wine capital.

terroir.learningPoint: Beaune's many premier cru climats make it a useful map for learning Burgundy hierarchy.

name: Pommard
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Pinot Noir red Burgundy. Use INAO for official rules.
officialRulesNote: Pommard is a Côte de Beaune village appellation for red wines.
commonPracticeNote: Often taught as fuller, firmer, and more tannic than Volnay.

terroir.learningPoint: Pommard is a classic contrast point for structured Côte de Beaune Pinot Noir.

name: Volnay
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Pinot Noir red Burgundy. Use INAO for official rules.
officialRulesNote: Volnay is a Côte de Beaune village appellation for red wines.
commonPracticeNote: Often described as elegant, perfumed, and lighter-framed than Pommard.

terroir.learningPoint: Volnay is a key map contrast with Pommard: finesse versus firmer structure.

name: Meursault
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Chardonnay white Burgundy. Use INAO for exact rules.
officialRulesNote: Meursault is a Côte de Beaune village appellation strongly associated with dry white wines.
commonPracticeNote: Often richer and broader than Puligny-Montrachet shorthand.

terroir.learningPoint: Meursault anchors the richer, nuttier side of Côte de Beaune Chardonnay study.

name: Puligny-Montrachet
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Chardonnay white Burgundy. Use INAO for official rules.
officialRulesNote: Puligny-Montrachet is a Côte de Beaune village appellation famous for dry white wines.
commonPracticeNote: Often described as precise, mineral, and elegant.
classificationContext: Important for Montrachet-family grand cru context.

terroir.learningPoint: Puligny is central to studying high-precision Côte de Beaune Chardonnay.

name: Chassagne-Montrachet
authorizedGrapesNote: Study shorthand: Chardonnay-dominant in global fine-wine context, with Pinot Noir also produced.
officialRulesNote: Chassagne-Montrachet is a Côte de Beaune village appellation for white and red wines.
commonPracticeNote: White wines are often broader and more powerful than Puligny shorthand.
classificationContext: Important for Montrachet-family grand cru context.

terroir.learningPoint: Chassagne helps complete the Meursault-Puligny-Chassagne white Burgundy study triangle.
